body.purpose: Theme-invariant humanist sans for an approachable technical workspace.

label.purpose: Tracked uppercase dock and inspector structure.

motion.name: control-transition
motion.value: background-color 160ms ease, border-color 160ms ease, color 160ms ease, box-shadow 160ms ease

components.name: Day Primary Action
components.description: Olive confirmation action for the warm binder theme.
components.css: .ds-day-primary { background:#647832; color:#fbf6ea; border:1px solid #647832; border-radius:5px; padding:6px 12px; font:700 12px/1.2 'Avenir Next',Avenir,'Segoe UI',sans-serif; cursor:pointer; } .ds-day-primary:hover { background:#71893a; } .ds-day-primary:active { background:#506128; } .ds-day-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #647832; outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Night Primary Action
components.description: Acid-lime confirmation action for the dark lighting-plot theme.
components.css: .ds-night-primary { background:#d7ff48; color:#101518; border:1px solid #d7ff48; border-radius:5px; padding:6px 12px; font:700 12px/1.2 'Avenir Next',Avenir,'Segoe UI',sans-serif; cursor:pointer; } .ds-night-primary:hover { background:#e5ff7a; } .ds-night-primary:active { background:#b8de35; } .ds-night-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #d7ff48; outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Theme Field
components.description: A role-driven inspector field; its surface, ink, and line switch together by theme.
components.css: .ds-field-label { display:grid; gap:8px; color:var(--ink,#41362d); font:700 10px/1.2 'Avenir Next',Avenir,'Segoe UI',sans-serif; letter-spacing:.14em; } .ds-field { background:var(--field,#fbf4e7); color:var(--ink-strong,#2e261f); border:1px solid var(--line-strong,#927d65); border-radius:5px; padding:8px 12px; font:600 14px/1.2 'Avenir Next',Avenir,'Segoe UI',sans-serif; } .ds-field:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--accent,#647832); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Production Header
components.description: The role-driven binder header shared by both themes.
components.html: ◼ Film Diagram StudioLIGHTING & CAMERA PRE-VIZ
components.css: .ds-header { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:16px; background:var(--binder,#4a382c); color:var(--ink-strong,#2e261f); border-bottom:1px solid var(--line,#b8a589); padding:12px 20px; font-family:'Avenir Next',Avenir,'Segoe UI',sans-serif; } .ds-header strong { display:block; font-size:18px; letter-spacing:.025em; } .ds-header small { display:block; color:var(--ink-muted,#766553); font-size:10px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:.14em; margin-top:4px; } .ds-header button { background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--binder,#4a382c) 82%,var(--control,#f1e6d1)); color:var(--ink-strong,#2e261f); border:1px solid var(--line,#b8a589); border-radius:6px; padding:6px 12px; font:700 12px/1.2 inherit; } .ds-header button:hover { background:var(--control-hover,#e8d8bc); } .ds-header button:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--accent,#647832); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Lighting Plot Frame
components.description: A user-configurable paper-like plot held inside the active theme’s binder frame.
components.html: SET A · DAY INT.●▶
components.css: .ds-stage { background:var(--workspace,#b8a98f); padding:20px; } .ds-plot { position:relative; min-height:180px; overflow:hidden; outline:10px solid var(--canvas-outline,#4a382c); background:#f5f1e7; background-image:repeating-linear-gradient(0deg,#c8c0b0 0,#c8c0b0 1px,transparent 1px,transparent 20px),repeating-linear-gradient(90deg,#c8c0b0 0,#c8c0b0 1px,transparent 1px,transparent 20px); border:1px solid var(--line,#b8a589); box-shadow:0 22px 56px rgba(52,37,26,.28),0 2px 8px rgba(52,37,26,.2); } .ds-plot-label { position:absolute; top:16px; left:16px; background:#1e40af; color:#f5f1e7; border-radius:3px; padding:4px 8px; font:700 10px/1.2 'Avenir Next',Avenir,'Segoe UI',sans-serif; letter-spacing:.08em; } .ds-light,.ds-camera { position:absolute; font:700 28px/1 sans-serif; } .ds-light { color:#3b82f6; top:80px; left:43%; } .ds-camera { color:#1e40af; top:112px; left:60%; }

narrative.overview:
Film Diagram Studio is an operating surface made for real production planning. Its visual system has two deliberate shifts: Day theme is a warm, earthy notebook and binder environment; Night theme is a dark lighting-plot workstation. Both preserve the same compact controls, three-zone workbench layout, and paper-like diagram as the primary object.

Theme changes are role substitutions, not a new identity. --workspace, --binder, --inspector, --control, --field, ink, line, accent, amber, danger, canvas-outline, and scroll roles each have a defined day and night value. Semantic colors within the drawing remain stable so a camera, light, or furniture mark never changes its meaning with the workspace theme.
keyCharacteristics: Day: tactile warm paper, walnut binder, olive confirmation, and handwritten-production-notebook warmth.
Night: blue-charcoal plot table, acid-lime confirmation, and high-contrast technical focus.
Compact, visibly bordered controls rather than card-heavy dashboard chrome.
A large, elevated canvas that remains the visual center in either shift.

rules.name: The Role-Swap Rule
rules.body: Theme code uses semantic CSS roles, never one-off theme hexes in components. A theme shift changes the role values, not the UI’s hierarchy or meaning.

rules.name: The Diagram-Stays-True Rule
rules.body: Diagram Navy, Diagram Blue, and Diagram Violet stay theme-invariant; application state uses the active theme accent instead.

rules.name: The Canvas-First Rule
rules.body: Preserve tools left, diagram center, and properties right. Panels may collapse, but the plot remains the visual and interaction priority.

rules.name: The Plot Is the Object Rule
rules.body: Do not give dock modules or inspector cards comparable elevation.

dos: Do switch complete semantic role families between Day and Night through CSS custom properties.
Do use olive active states on warm Day surfaces and lime active states on Night surfaces.
Do preserve the stable blue, navy, and violet legend for diagram objects in both themes.
Do keep controls compact, visibly bordered, and fast to scan.
Do reserve the strongest elevation and largest uninterrupted area for the plot.
donts: Don't hardcode a Day or Night neutral in a component when a role variable exists.
Don't mix warm Day surfaces with Night ink, lines, or accents (or the reverse) inside one active theme.
Don't use diagram blue as the application active-state color.
Don't spread amber or danger roles beyond their special-action and destructive meanings.
Don't turn theme switching into a layout, typography, or semantic-diagram change.
